context: The diagram starts with the heap already built as [5, 4, 3, 1, 1, 2]. It does not show the input order before heap construction. In a max-heap, every parent is at least as large as either child. After the heap is restored, its root is the largest active element.

The binary tree at upper left corresponds to the array below in level order, with indices starting at 0. The left and right children of index i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2, respectively. Only indices within the active range belong to the heap. Green nodes mark the active heap and gray nodes the sorted range on the right.
description: To extract the maximum, swap the root with the last (rightmost) element of the active heap. This places the maximum in the gray sorted suffix on the right. Then sift down from the root within the shortened green prefix only.

When a node turns gray and joins the sorted range, its connecting edge in the tree on the left disappears. It takes no further part in sift-down comparisons, but the element stays in place in the array below. Shrinking the heap removes no elements from the array.

frames.announcement: Start with a six-element max-heap whose root holds the maximum, 5.
frames.explanation: The active heap covers indices 0 through 5. Its root, 5 at index 0, has children 4 and 3. Both children of 4 are 1, and the left child of 3 is the last heap element, 2. Now nums = [5, 4, 3, 1, 1, 2], with no sorted suffix yet.
frames.key_state: Now nums = [5, 4, 3, 1, 1, 2]. The active heap range is [0, 5], and the sorted suffix is [].
frames.title: Initial max-heap built

frames.announcement: Swap the root, 5, with the last heap element, 2. Fix 5 at the end and shrink the active heap range.
frames.explanation: Swap the root, 5 at index 0, with the last heap element, 2 at index 5. The maximum, 5, is fixed at index 5 and turns gray. The new root, 2, is smaller than its children 4 and 3, so the heap needs a sift-down. Now nums = [2, 4, 3, 1, 1, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 4], and the sorted suffix is [5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [2, 4, 3, 1, 1, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 4], and the sorted suffix is [5].
frames.title: Swap the root, 5, to the end of the array

frames.announcement: Swap 4 into the root to restore the five-element max-heap.
frames.explanation: The root, 2, is smaller than its larger child, 4, so the heap needs repair. Of the root and its children 4 and 3, choose the largest, 4, and swap it with 2. At index 1, the 2 is at least as large as both its children, each 1, so it stops sinking. The five-element heap is restored. Now nums = [4, 2, 3, 1, 1, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 4], and the sorted suffix is [5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [4, 2, 3, 1, 1, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 4], and the sorted suffix is [5].
frames.title: Sift down to restore the five-element max-heap

frames.announcement: Swap the root, 4, with the last active element, 1. The sorted suffix grows to 4, 5.
frames.explanation: Swap the root, 4, with the 1 at the end of the active heap (index 4), fixing 4 at index 4. The new root, 1, is smaller than its children 2 and 3. Now nums = [1, 2, 3, 1, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 3], and the sorted suffix is [4, 5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [1, 2, 3, 1, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 3], and the sorted suffix is [4, 5].
frames.title: Swap the root, 4, to index 4

frames.announcement: Swap 3 into the root to restore the four-element max-heap.
frames.explanation: The root, 1, is smaller than its larger child, 3. Compare the root with its children 2 and 3. Swap the largest, the right child 3, with the root. The 1 moves down to index 2, a leaf, restoring the four-element max-heap. Now nums = [3, 2, 1, 1, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 3], and the sorted suffix is [4, 5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [3, 2, 1, 1, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 3], and the sorted suffix is [4, 5].
frames.title: Sift down to restore the four-element max-heap

frames.announcement: Swap the root, 3, with the last active element, 1, fixing 3 at index 3.
frames.explanation: Swap the root, 3, with the 1 at the end of the active heap (index 3), fixing 3 at the left end of the sorted suffix. The root, 1, is now smaller than its left child, 2. Now nums = [1, 2, 1, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 2], and the sorted suffix is [3, 4, 5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [1, 2, 1, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 2], and the sorted suffix is [3, 4, 5].
frames.title: Swap the root, 3, to index 3

frames.announcement: Swap 2 into the root to restore the three-element max-heap.
frames.explanation: The root, 1, is smaller than its larger child, 2, so the heap needs repair. Compare the root with its children 2 and 1. Swap the largest, the left child 2, with the root to restore the three-element heap [2, 1, 1]. Now nums = [2, 1, 1, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 2], and the sorted suffix is [3, 4, 5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [2, 1, 1, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 2], and the sorted suffix is [3, 4, 5].
frames.title: Sift down to restore the three-element max-heap

frames.announcement: Swap the root, 2, with the last active element, 1. The sorted suffix grows to 2, 3, 4, 5.
frames.explanation: Swap the root, 2, with the 1 at the end of the active heap (index 2), adding 2 to the sorted suffix. Both remaining elements are 1. Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 1], and the sorted suffix is [2, 3, 4, 5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 1], and the sorted suffix is [2, 3, 4, 5].
frames.title: Swap the root, 2, to index 2

frames.announcement: The root and left child are both 1, satisfying the max-heap property. This sift-down ends.
frames.explanation: In the two-element heap, the sift-down check compares the root, 1, with its left child, also 1. The parent is already at least as large as its child. The figure highlights the comparison path, but no swap occurs and the values stay the same. Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 1], and the sorted suffix is [2, 3, 4, 5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 1], and the sorted suffix is [2, 3, 4, 5]. The two 1s are equal, so the sift-down check made no swap.
frames.title: Equal 1s need no swap during the sift-down check

frames.announcement: Swap the two equal 1s and shrink the active heap to one element.
frames.explanation: Swap indices 0 and 1 in the two-element heap. Both hold 1, so the array values stay the same. The 1 at index 1 turns gray and joins the sorted suffix. Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 0], and the sorted suffix is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 0], and the sorted suffix is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The two 1s at indices 0 and 1 have been swapped. The values stay the same, and index 1 is fixed.
frames.title: Make the final swap between the root and last active element

frames.announcement: Check the single-node active heap. No swap is needed.
frames.explanation: The active heap now consists only of the root, 1 at index 0. It has no active child to compare, so sifting down ends immediately. The figure still highlights the root in green, with five gray items to its right. Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 0], and the sorted suffix is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
frames.key_state: Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap range is [0, 0], and the sorted suffix is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The single node has no active children, so the sift-down check ends immediately.
frames.title: A single-node heap needs no sift-down

frames.announcement: The last element needs no further work. All six elements are in ascending order.
frames.explanation: The last remaining element, 1 at index 0, is the array minimum and needs no extraction. It too turns gray, so all six elements are in the sorted range. Now nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. The active heap awaiting processing is empty, and all six items are sorted.
frames.key_state: Sorting is complete. All six elements of nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] are in place.
frames.title: The last element is already in place, completing the sort

summary: Build a max-heap, then repeatedly swap its root with the last active element and shrink the heap. This sorts the six elements into [1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].
title: In-place heap sort: move each maximum to the right end
